title: observability: add token-level KV metrics + tracing, update dashboards and alert tuning
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: teams have asked for finer-grained cost and latency breakdowns to correlate KV cache behavior with per-token latency and unit cost. Motivation: reduce alert noise by surfacing token-level regressions (e.g. token-level cache misses, slow token generation) and provide actionable dashboards for SREs and runtime engineers. What this PR does: 1) adds Prometheus metrics for token-level KV cache hit/miss rates and token generation latency with a token_pos_bucket label to keep cardinality bounded; 2) instruments tokenization, KV lookup and per-token generation paths with lightweight tracing spans and configurable sampling; 3) updates Grafana dashboards to include token-level panels for cost, latency, and cache hit heatmaps; 4) tunes alerting rules and adds a short suppression window to reduce false positives from transient spikes; 5) documents the new metrics and provides a short runbook for investigating token-level alerts. Implementation notes: token_pos_bucket uses boundaries (0,1-8,9-64,65+) and is exposed on histograms/metrics to avoid high-cardinality; tracing spans are gated behind a sampling flag and are no-op when sampling is disabled; dashboard variables default to model and route and include sane time ranges. Checklist: - [x] Prometheus metrics and recording rules - [x] Tracing spans + sampling config - [x] Grafana dashboard JSON + panels - [x] Alert rule updates and suppression window - [x] Docs and runbook updates - [x] Unit + integration tests added/updated
